unit.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Algebra
unit.act: Act XIII - Describing multiplicative change and undoing it
unit.role: Complete the Algebra course with repeated proportional change, inverse exponentiation, and equation solving.
unit.governingQuestion: How do we describe multiplicative change and solve for an unknown exponent?
unit.storyArc: Constant differences are contrasted with constant ratios. Repeated percentages produce exponential models, compounding motivates e, and logarithms reverse exponentiation. Log laws follow from exponent laws and solve previously inaccessible equations.
outcomes: Construct and interpret exponential growth and decay models.
Use compound and continuous growth formulas.
Define logarithms as inverse exponentiation and use log laws.
Solve exponential and logarithmic equations with domain checks.
unit.investigation: Compare linear, exponential, and logarithmic claims made from the same data and decide which conclusions are justified.
unit.mastery: Students construct models, solve exact and approximate equations, and reject logarithmic candidates outside the domain.
